## Figure 1.10: Average Terms on New External Debt Commitments for IDA-Eligible Countries, by Creditor Type, 2015–25
Line chart, two panels.

- **Panels:**  
  - **a. Private Creditors**  
  - **b. Official Creditors**
- **Time span:** 2015–2025
- **Series / legend:**  
  - **Grace period**  
  - **Maturity**  
  - **Interest (right axis)**
- **Left axis (both panels):** **Grace period and maturity (years)**, range **0 to 40**
- **Right axis (both panels):** **Percent**, range **0 to 9**

### Panel a. Private Creditors
Approximate values read from the line positions, except where the text explicitly states the 2025 interest rate.

| Year | Grace period (years) | Maturity (years) | Interest, right axis (%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2015 | ≈7.2 | ≈9.4 | ≈6.1 |
| 2016 | ≈4.4 | ≈8.4 | ≈5.3 |
| 2017 | ≈7.6 | ≈11.2 | ≈5.7 |
| 2018 | ≈8.9 | ≈12.8 | ≈6.0 |
| 2019 | ≈8.9 | ≈14.2 | ≈5.8 |
| 2020 | ≈8.5 | ≈13.7 | ≈3.9 |
| 2021 | ≈8.2 | ≈11.5 | ≈5.0 |
| 2022 | ≈4.0 | ≈10.3 | ≈4.9 |
| 2023 | ≈3.6 | ≈10.8 | ≈6.6 |
| 2024 | ≈5.3 | ≈8.0 | ≈7.6 |
| 2025 | ≈5.1 | ≈11.2 | **8.2** |

**Visually verifiable patterns and comparisons**
- **Interest rates** for private creditors are the highest series movement in the figure and rise sharply after 2022, reaching the panel high in **2025 (8.2%)**.
- The **lowest private-creditor interest rate** is around **2020 (≈3.9%)**.
- **Maturity** under private creditors peaks around **2019 (≈14.2 years)**, then shortens, especially in **2024 (≈8.0 years)**, before rebounding in **2025**.
- **Grace period** is longest around **2018–19 (≈8.9 years)** and shortest around **2023 (≈3.6 years)**.
- In every year shown, **maturity exceeds grace period**.

### Panel b. Official Creditors
Approximate values read from the line positions.

| Year | Grace period (years) | Maturity (years) | Interest, right axis (%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2015 | ≈6.2 | ≈25.5 | ≈1.6 |
| 2016 | ≈6.4 | ≈24.8 | ≈1.9 |
| 2017 | ≈5.8 | ≈24.8 | ≈1.9 |
| 2018 | ≈6.2 | ≈24.3 | ≈2.0 |
| 2019 | ≈5.4 | ≈22.8 | ≈2.2 |
| 2020 | ≈5.8 | ≈25.5 | ≈1.6 |
| 2021 | ≈5.2 | ≈23.7 | ≈1.6 |
| 2022 | ≈5.4 | ≈24.8 | ≈1.8 |
| 2023 | ≈5.7 | ≈24.1 | ≈3.0 |
| 2024 | ≈6.7 | ≈25.9 | ≈2.7 |
| 2025 | ≈6.1 | ≈24.5 | ≈2.7 |

**Visually verifiable patterns and comparisons**
- **Official-creditor interest rates** remain much lower than private-creditor rates throughout the period, mostly around **1.6%–2.2%** until the jump in **2023**.
- The **highest official-creditor interest rate** appears in **2023 (≈3.0%)**, easing slightly in **2024–25 (≈2.7%)**.
- **Maturity** for official creditors stays long and relatively stable, generally around **23–26 years**, much longer than for private creditors in every year.
- **Grace periods** for official creditors are fairly stable, mostly around **5–7 years**, with a local high in **2024 (≈6.7 years)**.
- Compared with panel a, official-creditor terms show **longer maturities and lower interest rates** across the full period.

**Cross-panel comparison**
- **Private-creditor interest rates** are consistently and substantially above **official-creditor interest rates**.
- **Official-creditor maturities** are consistently much longer than **private-creditor maturities**.
- By **2025**, the contrast is especially sharp: private-creditor interest is **8.2%**, versus roughly **2.7%** for official creditors.

**Source:** World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
